Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — QuantHealth is excited about Redwood's inference performance. We're about to finalize commercial terms for the enterprise deal (QH-4782) and need a small set of custom SLA addenda and order form language before procurement can sign.

High-level asks:
- Availability target: 99.95% across our primary regions (us-east-1 + us-west-2) with a regional failover plan.
- Latency commitments: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 350ms for standard small/medium models under normal traffic.
- Credit calculation: want explicit formula tied to minute-level measured downtime and a cap tied to monthly subscription.
- Evidence & telemetry: retention of telemetry/audit logs for 90 days and a runbook for incident evidence (synthetic checks + request traces).

We attached the draft order form and our MSA redlines. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept an Availability Annex exhibit and include the credit formula in the order form (we prefer an explicit per-minute credit schedule)? Also: can you confirm the evidence path (who provides telemetry extracts) and whether exception language for burst traffic or maintenance windows is negotiable?

Attachments: QH-4782_OrderForm_Draft.pdf; QuantHealth_MSA_Redlines.docx

Appreciate a phone sync if helpful — procurement target is to finish redlines by EOW for our legal.

Hi Samantha — thanks for the detailed note and the drafts. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Karthik (solutions/ops) so we can align on a single redline and evidence path.

High-level response: we can generally support an Availability Annex as an exhibit to the Order Form, and we typically include an explicit credit schedule tied to measured availability. There are a few knobs we need to confirm with you:
1) Expected steady-state and peak QPS (helps us size any recommended dedicated capacity).
2) Whether you require a guaranteed p99 at scale, or if you accept a model-variant fallback (e.g., slightly smaller quantized model) for degraded capacity scenarios.
3) Any constrained maintenance blackout windows you need (we have standard weekly maintenance windows; bespoke carveouts are possible).

Proposed next steps: Karthik will propose order form language and an ops evidence plan within 3 business days. Kimberly — can you please review the attached MSA redlines and flag any legal no-go items, especially around the credit cap and evidence disclosure?

I've attached a working redline for the Availability Annex that Karthik and I will iterate on: redline_availability_annex_v1.docx

If it's helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the proposed credit calculation.

Samantha / Stephanie / Kimberly — quick technical proposal from the ops side. Below are the recommended order form & evidence items to include in the Availability Annex. Please treat these as a starting point; we can tighten language after we see traffic numbers.

Suggested Order Form language (summary):
- Availability definition: API availability measured at the account level for inference endpoints (successful 200-series responses / total requests) aggregated per-minute. Regional availability is computed per-region; global availability computed as weighted average by traffic.
- Measurement windows & credits: If availability for any calendar month falls below 99.95%, credits computed as: credit = (99.95% - measured_availability) / 0.05% * monthly_subscription_fee * 0.10, with a monthly cap of 50% of monthly_subscription_fee. (We can insert a table for minute-level outages rather than just a formula.)
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 350ms under agreed traffic profile. Exception when falling back to alternate model/quantized variant during capacity degradation — the fallback path must be called out in the annex.
- Burst & maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance windows (standard weekly window) excluded; documented spike protection for traffic bursts for up to 10 minutes — beyond that, capacity-based limits apply unless Dedicated capacity is purchased.

Evidence & operational runbook:
- Redwood to provide synthetic-check summaries, request traces, and audit logs with 90-day retention for SLA evidence.
- For any credit claim, QuantHealth provides request IDs/time ranges; Redwood will provide telemetry extracts and a joint post-incident review within 10 business days.
- If customer requests Dedicated capacity guarantees (reserved pool), we will include a provisioning lead time and a separate capacity SLA.

Attachments: ops_runbook_sla_evidence.pdf (ops evidence checklist + sample telemetry extracts)

Questions for QuantHealth:
- Can you share a 7-day tail distribution of request sizes and peak QPS?
- Will you consider a hybrid approach: default hosted with ability to opt-in to Dedicated for high-throughput endpoints?

I can produce a versioned redline of the Order Form (credit table + exceptions) once we get the traffic profile.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
